# `silk/color/color`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

Colors in the CSS Color 4 color spaces, with conversion, gamut mapping, mixing, adjustment, and
contrast measurement.

## When to use
Use [`Color`](#Color) whenever a color is more than four channels to copy: to convert between sRGB,
Display P3, Oklch, Lab, HSL, and the other [`ColorSpace`](#ColorSpace) values, to interpolate gradient stops,
to derive hover and pressed shades of a theme color, or to check that text is readable on its
background. Use [`to`](#Color.impl.to) to convert, [`toGamut`](#Color.impl.toGamut) or [`toRgba`](#Color.impl.toRgba) to get displayable channels,
[`mix`](#Color.impl.mix) to interpolate, [`lighten`](#Color.impl.lighten), [`darken`](#Color.impl.darken), [`saturate`](#Color.impl.saturate), and [`rotateHue`](#Color.impl.rotateHue) to adjust, and
[`contrastRatio`](#Color.impl.contrastRatio) to measure legibility.

## Details
A color is a [`ColorSpace`](#ColorSpace), three components, and an alpha, all public and in `f64`. Components
use the CSS Color 4 reference ranges, except that percentages are fractions in `[0, 1]`:

- RGB spaces (`Srgb`, `SrgbLinear`, `DisplayP3`, `A98Rgb`, `ProphotoRgb`, `Rec2020`): red,
  green, and blue in `[0, 1]` inside the gamut.
- `XyzD65` and `XyzD50`: X, Y, and Z, with Y `1` for the reference white.
- `Lab`: lightness in `[0, 100]`, then a and b, roughly in `[-125, 125]`. `Lch`: lightness,
  chroma from `0`, then hue in degrees.
- `Oklab`: lightness in `[0, 1]`, then a and b, roughly in `[-0.4, 0.4]`. `Oklch`: lightness,
  chroma from `0`, then hue in degrees.
- `Hsl`: hue in degrees, saturation and lightness in `[0, 1]`. `Hwb`: hue in degrees, whiteness
  and blackness in `[0, 1]`.

A NaN component or alpha is a missing component, which CSS writes as `none`. Conversion reads a
missing component as zero. [`mix`](#Color.impl.mix) instead takes it from the other color, as CSS Color 4
interpolation requires. Conversion into a polar space marks the hue of an achromatic color, such
as white or gray, as missing, because no hue describes it.

Conversion goes through CIE XYZ with the D65 white point, using the matrices and transfer
functions of the CSS Color 4 sample code. Lab and ProPhoto use a D50 white and a Bradford
adaptation. Conversion never clips: a color outside the gamut of the target space gets
components outside `[0, 1]`. [`toGamut`](#Color.impl.toGamut) and [`toRgba`](#Color.impl.toRgba) map it into the gamut with the CSS Color
4 algorithm, which lowers Oklch chroma until the color fits and keeps lightness and hue.

## Gotchas
Missing components are NaN, so `==` on two components or a direct arithmetic step can give NaN.
Read a hue through [`isMissing`](#Color.impl.isMissing) first, or use [`approxEquals`](#Color.impl.approxEquals), which treats two missing
components as equal.

## Examples
### Derive theme shades and check text contrast
```silk
import silk.color.color { Color, ColorSpace, Interpolation }

pub fn main() -> i32 {
  let brand = Color.fromHex(0x3366cc)
  let hover = brand.lighten(0.08)
  let border = brand.mix(Color.white(), 0.5, Interpolation.new(ColorSpace.Oklab))
  if hover.space != ColorSpace.Srgb || border.space != ColorSpace.Oklab {
    return 1
  }
  if Color.white().contrastRatio(brand) < 4.5 {
    return 2
  }
  let channels = brand.to(ColorSpace.Oklch).toRgba()
  if channels.b < 0.79 || channels.b > 0.81 {
    return 3
  }
  return 0
}
```

## See also
Use `silk.color.rgba` for plain straight or premultiplied channels, and `silk.color.srgb` for
the sRGB transfer function alone.

Import as `Color` with `import silk.color.color { Color }`.

<a id="Interpolation"></a>

## `Interpolation`

```silk
pub struct Interpolation
```

The color space and hue method in which [`mix`](#Color.impl.mix) interpolates two colors.

### When to use

Use `Interpolation.new(ColorSpace.Oklab)` for even gradients without hue shifts, which is the
CSS default. Use `ColorSpace.Oklch` to keep colors saturated through the middle of a gradient,
and `ColorSpace.SrgbLinear` to match physical light mixing.

### Details

The fields are public. A hue method only affects polar spaces: `Lch`, `Oklch`, `Hsl`, and `Hwb`.

```silk
pub space: ColorSpace
```

The color space in which components are interpolated, and the space of the result.

<a id="Interpolation.hue"></a>

### Field `hue`

```silk
pub hue: HueInterpolation
```

The arc taken around the hue circle in a polar space.

<a id="Color"></a>

## `Color`

```silk
pub struct Color
```

A color: three components in a [`ColorSpace`](#ColorSpace) and an alpha.

### When to use

Use `Color` to convert between color spaces, map wide-gamut colors to a display, interpolate
gradient stops, derive shades, and measure contrast. Use `silk.color.rgba.Rgba` for channels
that only need to be stored or uploaded.

### Details

The fields are public. Component ranges depend on `space`: RGB spaces use `[0, 1]`, `Lab` and
`Lch` lightness use `[0, 100]`, `Oklab` and `Oklch` lightness use `[0, 1]`, hues are in degrees,
and HSL and HWB percentages are fractions in `[0, 1]`. Alpha is in `[0, 1]` and straight, not
premultiplied.

A NaN component or alpha is missing, as CSS `none`: conversion reads it as zero and [`mix`](#Color.impl.mix)
takes the value from the other color. Conversion into a polar space marks the hue of an
achromatic color as missing.

### Gotchas

Two missing components are NaN and never compare equal with `==`. Compare colors with
[`approxEquals`](#Color.impl.approxEquals).

<a id="Color.space"></a>

### Field `space`

```silk
pub space: ColorSpace
```

The color space that gives `components` their meaning.

<a id="Color.components"></a>

### Field `components`

```silk
pub components: [f64; 3]
```

The three components in the order CSS writes them for `space`. NaN marks a missing component.

<a id="Color.alpha"></a>

### Field `alpha`

```silk
pub alpha: f64
```

The opacity in `[0, 1]`, straight rather than premultiplied. NaN marks a missing alpha.

<a id="Color.impl.to"></a>

### Method `to`

```silk
pub fn to(self: Self, space: ColorSpace) -> Color
```

Returns the color converted to `space`, without gamut mapping.

#### Details

Missing components read as zero, and alpha is copied, including a missing alpha. A conversion
to the same space returns the color unchanged. A conversion into `Lch`, `Oklch`, `Hsl`, or
`Hwb` marks the hue missing when the color is achromatic. The result can lie outside the gamut
of `space`; use [`toGamut`](#Color.impl.toGamut) to bring it inside.

Conversion among `Srgb`, `SrgbLinear`, `Hsl`, and `Hwb`, between `Lab` and `Lch`, and between
`Oklab` and `Oklch` uses the direct formulas. Every other conversion goes through CIE XYZ
(D65).

<a id="Color.impl.inGamut"></a>

### Method `inGamut`

```silk
pub fn inGamut(self: Self, space: ColorSpace) -> bool
```

Returns `true` when the color lies inside the gamut of `space`, within `1e-9` per channel.

#### Details

For an RGB space, every channel must be in `[0, 1]`. `Hsl` and `Hwb` use the sRGB gamut.
`Lab`, `Lch`, `Oklab`, `Oklch`, `XyzD50`, and `XyzD65` hold every color, so the result is
`true`.

<a id="Color.impl.toGamut"></a>

### Method `toGamut`

```silk
pub fn toGamut(self: Self, space: ColorSpace) -> Color
```

Returns the color converted to `space` and mapped into its gamut with the CSS Color 4
algorithm.

#### When to use

Use `toGamut` before displaying a color from a wider space, such as an Oklch value with high
chroma or a Display P3 color on an sRGB screen.

#### Details

A color already inside the gamut is converted exactly. Otherwise the algorithm keeps Oklch
lightness and hue, and searches for the largest chroma whose clipped color is within a just
noticeable difference (`deltaEOK` of `0.02`) of the unclipped one. Lightness of `1` or more
maps to white and `0` or less to black. `Hsl` and `Hwb` map into the sRGB gamut. Spaces
without a gamut (`Lab`, `Lch`, `Oklab`, `Oklch`, `XyzD50`, `XyzD65`) return the plain
conversion. Alpha is copied unchanged.

<a id="Color.impl.toRgba"></a>

### Method `toRgba`

```silk
pub fn toRgba(self: Self) -> Rgba<f64>
```

Returns the straight-alpha gamma-encoded sRGB channels of the color, mapped into the sRGB
gamut.

#### When to use

Use `toRgba` to hand a color to a CSS-style renderer or to pack it into bytes. Use
[`toLinearRgba`](#Color.impl.toLinearRgba) for linear-light blending and GPU pipelines.

#### Details

The color is mapped with the CSS Color 4 gamut-mapping algorithm, so every channel is in
`[0, 1]`. A missing alpha becomes `1`, and alpha is clamped to `[0, 1]`.

<a id="Color.impl.toLinearRgba"></a>

### Method `toLinearRgba`

```silk
pub fn toLinearRgba(self: Self) -> Rgba<f64>
```

Returns the straight-alpha linear-light sRGB channels of the color, mapped into the sRGB
gamut.

#### When to use

Use `toLinearRgba` for physically based blending and for GPU pipelines that render to an sRGB
surface format. Premultiply the result before compositing.

#### Details

The color is mapped with the CSS Color 4 gamut-mapping algorithm, so every channel is in
`[0, 1]`. A missing alpha becomes `1`, and alpha is clamped to `[0, 1]`.

<a id="Color.impl.mix"></a>

### Method `mix`

```silk
pub fn mix(self: Self, other: Color, t: f64, interpolation: Interpolation) -> Color
```

Returns the color `t` of the way from `self` to `other`, interpolated as CSS Color 4
specifies.

#### When to use

Use `mix` for gradient stops, transitions, and blends between theme colors. `t = 0.5` with
`Interpolation.new(ColorSpace.Oklab)` is CSS `color-mix(in oklab, self, other)`.

#### Details

The result is in `interpolation.space`. Both colors are converted to that space. A component
missing in one color takes the other's value, including a missing component carried over from
an analogous component of the original space, such as a missing hue or lightness. Components
are premultiplied by alpha (except hue), interpolated linearly, and divided by the
interpolated alpha. Hues follow `interpolation.hue`. `t` outside `[0, 1]` extrapolates.

#### Gotchas

The result is not gamut mapped. Call [`toGamut`](#Color.impl.toGamut) or [`toRgba`](#Color.impl.toRgba) before display, because an
interpolation in `Oklch` or `Lab` can leave the sRGB gamut.

<a id="Color.impl.lighten"></a>

### Method `lighten`

```silk
pub fn lighten(self: Self, amount: f64) -> Color
```

Returns the color with Oklch lightness raised by `amount`, in the color's own space.

#### When to use

Use `lighten` for hover states and lighter palette steps. Because Oklch lightness is
perceptual, the same `amount` looks like the same step for every hue.

#### Details

The color is converted to Oklch, lightness becomes `l + amount` clamped to `[0, 1]`, and the
result is converted back to the original space. Chroma and hue are unchanged, so a light,
saturated result can leave the gamut of an RGB space; call [`toGamut`](#Color.impl.toGamut) before display.

<a id="Color.impl.darken"></a>

### Method `darken`

```silk
pub fn darken(self: Self, amount: f64) -> Color
```

Returns the color with Oklch lightness lowered by `amount`, in the color's own space.

#### When to use

Use `darken` for pressed states and darker palette steps.

#### Details

The color is converted to Oklch, lightness becomes `l - amount` clamped to `[0, 1]`, and the
result is converted back to the original space. Chroma and hue are unchanged; call [`toGamut`](#Color.impl.toGamut)
before display.

<a id="Color.impl.saturate"></a>

### Method `saturate`

```silk
pub fn saturate(self: Self, amount: f64) -> Color
```

Returns the color with Oklch chroma raised by `amount`, in the color's own space.

#### Details

The color is converted to Oklch, chroma becomes `c + amount` with a floor of zero, and the
result is converted back. Oklch chroma of saturated sRGB colors is about `0.1` to `0.32`, so
useful amounts are small, such as `0.02`. An achromatic color has no hue, so it gains chroma
toward a hue of zero (pink). The result can leave the gamut of an RGB space; call [`toGamut`](#Color.impl.toGamut)
before display.

<a id="Color.impl.desaturate"></a>

### Method `desaturate`

```silk
pub fn desaturate(self: Self, amount: f64) -> Color
```

Returns the color with Oklch chroma lowered by `amount`, with a floor of zero, in the color's
own space.

#### Details

The color is converted to Oklch, chroma becomes `max(c - amount, 0)`, and the result is
converted back. Lightness and hue are unchanged.

<a id="Color.impl.rotateHue"></a>

### Method `rotateHue`

```silk
pub fn rotateHue(self: Self, degrees: f64) -> Color
```

Returns the color with its Oklch hue turned by `degrees`, in the color's own space.

#### Details

The color is converted to Oklch, the hue becomes `h + degrees` wrapped into `[0, 360)`, and
the result is converted back. An achromatic color is returned unchanged in value. Rotating by
`180` gives the complementary color at the same lightness and chroma, which can leave the
gamut of an RGB space.

<a id="Color.impl.grayscale"></a>

### Method `grayscale`

```silk
pub fn grayscale(self: Self) -> Color
```

Returns the gray with the same Oklch lightness, in the color's own space.

#### Details

Oklch chroma becomes zero, so the result has the perceived lightness of the original. In a
polar space the hue of the result is missing.

<a id="Color.impl.invert"></a>

### Method `invert`

```silk
pub fn invert(self: Self) -> Color
```

Returns the sRGB negative of the color, in the color's own space.

#### Details

The color is mapped into the sRGB gamut, each gamma-encoded channel becomes `1 - channel`, and
the result is converted back. Alpha is unchanged. This matches the CSS `invert(1)` filter.

<a id="Color.impl.relativeLuminance"></a>

### Method `relativeLuminance`

```silk
pub fn relativeLuminance(self: Self) -> f64
```

Returns the WCAG 2 relative luminance of the color, from `0` for black to `1` for white.

#### Details

The color is mapped into the sRGB gamut, decoded to linear light, and weighted by
`0.2126 R + 0.7152 G + 0.0722 B`. Alpha is ignored; composite a translucent color over its
background first.

<a id="Color.impl.contrastRatio"></a>

### Method `contrastRatio`

```silk
pub fn contrastRatio(self: Self, other: Color) -> f64
```

Returns the WCAG 2 contrast ratio between the two colors, from `1` for equal luminance to `21`
for black on white.

#### When to use

Use `contrastRatio` to check text legibility. WCAG AA asks for at least `4.5` for body text
and `3` for large text and interface components; AAA asks for `7` and `4.5`.

#### Details

The ratio is `(lighter + 0.05) / (darker + 0.05)` of the two relative luminances, so the order
of the colors does not matter. Alpha is ignored; composite translucent colors first.

<a id="Color.impl.deltaEOK"></a>

### Method `deltaEOK`

```silk
pub fn deltaEOK(self: Self, other: Color) -> f64
```

Returns the CSS Color 4 `deltaEOK` difference: the Euclidean distance between the two colors
in Oklab.

#### When to use

Use `deltaEOK` to ask whether two colors look the same. A value below `0.02` is about one just
noticeable difference.

#### Details

Missing components read as zero. Alpha is ignored.

<a id="Color.impl.approxEquals"></a>

### Method `approxEquals`

```silk
pub fn approxEquals(self: Self, other: Color, tolerance: f64) -> bool
```

Returns `true` when both colors are in the same space and every component and alpha differ by
at most `tolerance`.

#### Details

Two missing components compare equal, and a missing component never equals a present one. Hues
compare around the circle, so `359.9` and `0.1` differ by `0.2`. Colors in different spaces
are never equal; convert one with [`to`](#Color.impl.to) first.
